					<h1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading mw-first-heading"><span class="mw-page-title-main">Murray G. Ross</span></h1>

					<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">
</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none">Canadian academic (1910–2000)</div>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1320445320">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">For the New Zealand sailor, see <a href="/wiki/Murray_Ross_(sailor)" title="Murray Ross (sailor)">Murray Ross (sailor)</a>.</div>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1316064257">.mw-parser-output .infobox-subbox{padding:0;border:none;margin:-3px;width:auto;min-width:100%;font-size:100%;clear:none;float:none;background-color:transparent;color:inherit}.mw-parser-output .infobox-3cols-child{margin:-3px}.mw-parser-output .infobox .navbar{font-size:100%}@media screen{html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .infobox-full-data:not(.notheme)>div:not(.notheme)[style]{background:#1f1f23!important;color:#f8f9fa}}@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme:dark){html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .infobox-full-data:not(.notheme)>div:not(.notheme)[style]{background:#1f1f23!important;color:#f8f9fa}}@media(min-width:640px){body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table{display:table!important}body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table>caption{display:table-caption!important}body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table>tbody{display:table-row-group}body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table th,body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table td{padding-left:inherit;padding-right:inherit}}</style><table class="infobox vcard"><tbody><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-above" style="font-size: 100%;"><div class="fn" style="font-size:125%;">Murray George Ross</div><div class="honorific-suffix" style="font-weight: normal;">O.C., O.Ont.</div></th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1316064257" /></td></tr><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-header" style="color: #202122; background:lavender;line-height:normal;padding:0.2em;"><a href="/wiki/University_president" class="mw-redirect" title="University president">President</a> of <a href="/wiki/York_University" title="York University">York University</a></th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data" style="border-bottom:none"><span class="nowrap"><b>In office</b></span><br />1959–1970</td><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1316064257" /></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label" style="text-align:left"><span class="nowrap">Succeeded by</span></th><td class="infobox-data"><a href="/wiki/David_W._Slater" title="David W. Slater">David W. Slater</a></td></tr><tr style="display:none"><td colspan="2">
</td></tr><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-header" style="color: #202122; background:lavender">Personal details</th></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Born</th><td class="infobox-data"><span style="display:none">(<span class="bday">1910-04-12</span>)</span>April 12, 1910<br /><div class="birthplace"><a href="/wiki/Sydney,_Nova_Scotia" title="Sydney, Nova Scotia">Sydney</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nova_Scotia" title="Nova Scotia">Nova Scotia</a></div></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Died</th><td class="infobox-data">July 20, 2000<span style="display:none">(2000-07-20)</span> (aged&#160;90)</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Nationality</th><td class="infobox-data"><a href="/wiki/Canadians" title="Canadians">Canadian</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label"><a href="/wiki/Alma_mater" title="Alma mater">Alma mater</a></th><td class="infobox-data"><a href="/wiki/Acadia_University" title="Acadia University">Acadia University</a>, <a href="/wiki/University_of_Toronto" title="University of Toronto">University of Toronto</a></td></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-below" style="border-top: 1px solid right;"><div></div></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><b>Murray George Ross</b>, <span class="nobold noexcerpt nowraplinks" style="font-size:;"><span style="font-size: 85%;"><a href="/wiki/Order_of_Canada" title="Order of Canada">OC</a></span>&#32;<span style="font-size: 85%;"><a href="/wiki/Order_of_Ontario" title="Order of Ontario">OOnt</a></span></span> (April 12, 1910 &#8211; July 20, 2000) was a Canadian sociologist, author, and academic administrator. He was the founding president of <a href="/wiki/Toronto" title="Toronto">Toronto</a>'s <a href="/wiki/York_University" title="York University">York University</a> and served in that role from 1959 to 1970.
</p><p>Born in <a href="/wiki/Sydney,_Nova_Scotia" title="Sydney, Nova Scotia">Sydney</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nova_Scotia" title="Nova Scotia">Nova Scotia</a>, the son of <a href="/wiki/James_Alway_Ross" title="James Alway Ross">James Alway Ross</a> and Sarah Agnes Kay,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ross received a <a href="/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts" title="Bachelor of Arts">Bachelor of Arts</a> degree in <a href="/wiki/Economics" title="Economics">economics</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sociology" title="Sociology">sociology</a> from <a href="/wiki/Acadia_University" title="Acadia University">Acadia University</a> in 1936. He received a <a href="/wiki/Master_of_Arts" title="Master of Arts">Master of Arts</a> degree in sociology from the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Toronto" title="University of Toronto">University of Toronto</a> in 1938. He did post-graduate work in sociology at the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Chicago" title="University of Chicago">University of Chicago</a> in 1939 and in <a href="/wiki/Social_psychology_(sociology)" title="Social psychology (sociology)">Social psychology</a> from <a href="/wiki/Columbia_University" title="Columbia University">Columbia University</a> in 1949. He received a <a href="/wiki/Legum_Doctor" class="mw-redirect" title="Legum Doctor">LL.D.</a> from the University of Toronto in 1971.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Who&#95;2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Who-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 1951, Ross was appointed an associate professor of Social Work at the University of Toronto. He became a professor in 1955. From 1956 to 1957, he was an Executive Assistant to the President and was a vice-president from 1957 to 1959. In 1959, he was appointed President of York University and served until 1970 when he became a professor of Social Science. He retired in 1972.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Who&#95;2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Who-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Honours">Honours</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Murray_G._Ross&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Honours"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In 1979, he was made an Officer of the <a href="/wiki/Order_of_Canada" title="Order of Canada">Order of Canada</a> "in recognition of his innovative leadership in the field of higher education".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He was awarded the <a href="/wiki/Order_of_Ontario" title="Order of Ontario">Order of Ontario</a> in 1988. He was awarded the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Centennial_Medal" title="Canadian Centennial Medal">Canadian Centennial Medal</a> and the <a href="/wiki/125th_Anniversary_of_the_Confederation_of_Canada_Medal" title="125th Anniversary of the Confederation of Canada Medal">125th Anniversary of the Confederation of Canada Medal</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Who&#95;2-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Who-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The Murray Ross Parkway, the Ross Building, and the Murray G. Ross (Valedictorian) Award at York University are named after him.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Selected_works">Selected works</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Murray_G._Ross&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Selected works"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<ul><li><i>Religious Beliefs of Youth: A Study and Analysis of the Structure and Function of the Religious Beliefs of Young Adults, Based on a Questionnaire Sample of 1,935 Youth and Intensive Interviews with 100 Young People</i> (Association Press, 1950)</li>
<li><i>The Y.M.C.A. in Canada: The Chronicle of a Century</i> (Ryerson Press, 1951)</li>
<li><i>New Understandings of Leadership: A Survey and Application of Research</i> with Charles E. Hendry (Association Press, 1957)</li>
<li><i>Case Histories in Community Organization</i> (Harper, 1958)</li>
<li><i>The new university</i> (University of Toronto Press, 1961)</li>
<li><i>New Universities in the Modern World</i> (St. Martin's Press, 1966)</li>
<li><i>Community Organization; Theory, Principles, and Practice</i> with B. W. Lappin (Harper &amp; Row, 1967)</li>
<li><i>The University: The Anatomy of Academe</i> (McGraw-Hill, 1976)</li>
<li><i>Canadian Corporate Directors on the Firing Line: On the Firing Line</i> (McGraw-Hill Ryerson, 1980)</li>
<li><i>The Way Must be Tried: Memoirs of a University Man</i> (Stoddart, 1992)</li></ul>
